record: roadmap F: validation of mid-fringe comparators against an exact ARMA(1,1) latent binary likelihood
status: DRAFT FOR REVIEW (note 28, revision 3) -- not frozen. No digest is binding. sid_run13.py must refuse every phase while status starts with DRAFT.

changes: NC6 compares W- and 2W-history filters on the same final observations; the extra pass is costed
every run stops at the earliest of 1.25 x prediction, the 7200 s point cap and the remaining aggregate budget; Gate 3 has an enforced 1800 s deadline including its first measurement
the builder refuses to overwrite a frozen protocol; verification stays read-only
one F-specific conda definition and channel policy for solve and installation; OpenBLAS pinned; pip packages locked separately
separate caveats for open, failed and validated closure
python pinned to 3.12.14 (review decision on r2 §11, option b); second dry-run solve recorded; stack checks, refusals and tests use the exact patch

closure wording no longer confines validation to C04 once any finite-window validation exists: before evaluation note 27's sentence; afterwards scope, campaign status and the validated, failed and unresolved tuples are reported separately

frozen_before: any ARMA likelihood evaluation, execution-stack numerical check, pilot or evaluation

adopted_choices.burn_in: W = max(1000, ceil(100 tau_c/c)), subject to the corrected NC6
adopted_choices.pilot: n_p = 125000 and stability factor 4, as planning choices; the variance bound is approximate
adopted_choices.checks: eight 50000-observation windows; simulator threshold 5 standard errors
adopted_choices.margins: prediction 1.10 and stop 1.25, subordinate to the enforced hard caps
adopted_choices.closure: K1 alone decides roadmap F; C08-boundary validation is reported separately

estimand.quantity: per-shot relative-entropy rate R of the theta = pi/2 binary record against the i.i.d. null p0 = 1/2; latent phase = finite-window integrated stationary OU phase
estimand.link: P(Y=1 | eps) = (1 + C cos(theta + eps))/2 = (1 - C sin eps)/2

K1.definition: six-term sinh-series Gaussian spectral rate with exact r_k = C^2 exp(-s^2) sinh(s^2 F(u) phi^k); 1024 midpoint frequencies omega = pi (j + 1/2)/1024
K1.source: analysis/runs/sid_run4.py gp_rate_series, read through the AST

K2.definition: geometric closed form with rho = r1/phi, r1 = C^2 exp(-s^2) sinh(s^2 F(u) phi)

K3.definition: geometric closed form with rho = r1/(F(u) phi)
K3.source: analysis/runs/sid_run3.py archived C08 map call, evaluated through the AST

K4.role: diagnostic control: point-sampled series, not a finite-window truth model

comparators.implementation_contract: the Gate-2 library must reproduce design_evidence comparator values to relative 1e-12 on the execution stack

reference_filter.latent_model: eps_n = x_n + b x_{n-1}; x_n = phi x_{n-1} + eta_n; eta_n ~ N(0, q)
reference_filter.parameters: phi = exp(-c/tau_c); F(u) = (cosh u - 1)/(u - 1 + exp(-u)); b = root with |b| < 1 of phi(1-F) b^2 + (1 + phi^2 - 2 F phi^2) b + phi(1-F) = 0; v_x = s^2/(1 + b^2 + 2 b phi); q = v_x (1 - phi^2)
reference_filter.grid: g_i = -L sqrt(v_x) + i 2 L sqrt(v_x)/(M - 1), i = 0..M-1
reference_filter.transition: T[i, i'] proportional to exp(-(g_i' - phi g_i)^2/(2 q)); every row normalised to 1
reference_filter.emission: E_y[i', i] = (1 + (2y - 1) C cos(theta + g_i' + b g_i))/2
reference_filter.stationary_initialisation: pi = left eigenvector of T for the eigenvalue nearest 1 (numpy.linalg.eig of T transpose, real part, normalised to sum 1); require sum|pi T - pi| <= 1e-12 and min(pi) >= -1e-15; entries in [-1e-15, 0) are set to 0 and pi is renormalised
reference_filter.first_step: at a pass's first observation m: alpha~_m(i, j) = pi(j) T[j, i] E_{y_m}(i, j)
reference_filter.recursion: beta(i) = sum_j alpha_{n-1}(i, j); alpha~_n(i', i) = T[i, i'] beta(i) E_{yn}(i', i); Z_n = sum alpha~_n; alpha_n = alpha~_n / Z_n
reference_filter.burn_in: W = max(1000, ceil(100 tau_c/c)) observations; the filter runs through them and every estimator excludes them
reference_filter.per_seed_estimator: pilot and evaluation passes start at observation 1; R_seed = mean of l_n over n = W+1 .. W+n
reference_filter.ar1_nesting_reference: same grid (with b = 0, so v_x = s^2), T, pi, emission, burn-in W and estimator: alpha~_1(i) = pi(i) E_{y1}(i); alpha~_n(i') = sum_i alpha_{n-1}(i) T[i, i'] E_{yn}(i')
reference_filter.committed_code_tie: the AR(1) reference with sid_lib.make_hmm's Gaussian-weight prior, one propagation by T before the first emission and W = 0 must reproduce sid_lib.hmm_rate(C, s, theta, phi, N, seed, M=121) to relative 1e-12 on hmm_rate's own record

simulator.method: exact OU in units of tau_c: standardised frequency z with unit variance and unit correlation time
simulator.window: over u: z <- e^{-u} z + xi_1 and I = (1 - e^{-u}) z_start + xi_2, with Var xi_1 = 1 - e^{-2u}, Var xi_2 = 2[u - 2(1 - e^{-u}) + (1 - e^{-2u})/2], Cov(xi_1, xi_2) = (1 - e^{-u})^2, drawn as the lower Cholesky factor times two standard normals
simulator.dead_time: over d = c/tau_c - u: z <- e^{-d} z + sqrt(1 - e^{-2d}) xi_3
simulator.outcome: y_n = 1 if U_n < (1 + C cos(theta + eps_n))/2
simulator.draw_order: z_0 = standard_normal(); then in blocks of 2^20 shots (the last block shorter): standard_normal((block, 3)) followed by random(block)
simulator.independence: uses neither phi nor b; the filter never sees the simulator's variables
simulator.scope: u > 0 only; the N0 nesting check uses sid_lib.simulate records

E1.role: C08 boundary at the archived C0 column nearest 0.4; winner tau of the archived map form at the stored threshold

E2.role: C08 boundary at the archived C0 column nearest 0.5; winner tau of the archived map form at the stored threshold

E3.role: stress validation point (per-shot C and s set directly; dead time 0.05 tau_c)

E4.role: stress validation point (per-shot C and s set directly; dead time 0.05 tau_c)

E5.role: stress validation point (per-shot C and s set directly; dead time 0.05 tau_c)

deferred.E6: (C, s, u, c/tau_c) = (0.4, 1.0, 0.30, 0.35): K1 and K2 differ by 5.6 %, inside the band, so it supplies no forced-incompatibility control (note 27)

NC2_simulator.statistics: sample variance of eps against s^2; lag-k autocorrelation against F(u) phi^k for k = 1..5
NC2_simulator.pass: |mean over seeds - exact| <= 5 x across-seed standard error, for every statistic

NC3_series.pass: K1 and K4 change by at most 1e-6 relative from (6 terms, 1024 frequencies) to (12 terms, 4096 frequencies)

NC4_stationary.pass: stationary_initialisation requirements on every grid used

records_for_NC5_NC6.initialisation: each pass starts from the stationary distribution at its first observation, runs through the observations before the estimation window as burn-in and is estimated over the same final observations
records_for_NC5_NC6.cost_per_seed: simulation 2W + 50000; M241_L7: (2W + 50000) + (W + 50000) filter steps; M241_L5, M121_L7 and M121_L5: W + 50000 each

NC5_grid.pass: for each pair, |mean paired difference| + t_{0.975,7} x its standard error <= 0.001 K1

NC6_finite_history.pass: |mean paired difference| + t_{0.975,7} x its standard error <= 0.001 K1
NC6_finite_history.meaning: the same final observations, filtered after W versus 2W preceding observations; only the history length differs

numerical_checks.failure: a failed check marks the point NUMERICAL_CHECK_FAILED: no pilot, no evaluation, no verdict. NC1 failure blocks every point. Grid, burn-in, record length and seeds change only through a superseding protocol version.

pilot.per_seed: W burn-in + n_p = 125000 post-burn-in shots on the evaluation grid
pilot.recorded: per-seed wall time and shots; across-seed sample variance S^2 of per-seed means; pooled batch-means variance for B = 10 and B = 20 equal batches; t_step = total filter-plus-simulation seconds / total shots including burn-in
pilot.not_recorded: per-seed means, their average, any comparator ratio
pilot.variance_bound: approximate conservative planning bound, not an exact confidence limit: U = max(U_seed, U_bm10, U_bm20); U_seed = 15 S^2 / chi2_{0.05,15}; U_bmB = vbar_B df_B / chi2_{0.05,df_B}, vbar_B = mean over seeds of var(batch means, ddof=1)/B, df_B = 16 (B - 1). The chi-square factors treat per-seed and batch means as approximately normal and batches as approximately independent
pilot.stability: if the largest of (S^2, vbar_10, vbar_20) exceeds 4 times the smallest, the point is PILOT_UNSTABLE and is not evaluated

shot_rule.total: N = 16 n_e post-burn-in shots, plus 16 W burn-in shots
shot_rule.no_topups: n_e is fixed before evaluation starts; no extension, replacement seed or early stop based on measured means
shot_rule.blindness: only K1 (deterministic) and the pilot variance bound enter n_e
shot_rule.constants_source: t, z and chi-square quantiles are read from this protocol's constants block and never recomputed on the execution stack; SciPy 1.10 and 1.17 already differ by 2.5e-10 relative in t(0.975, 7)
shot_rule.note: planned N does not decide a verdict; the realised interval does

evaluation.admission: a mandatory point is evaluated only if predicted_seconds <= 7200 and <= the remaining aggregate budget; E1 and E2 only together, if both passed their checks and pilots, each predicted <= 7200 s and their sum <= the remaining budget

rule: NO_VERDICT if the point failed a numerical check, was PILOT_UNSTABLE, not attempted or INCOMPLETE
VALIDATED if Q lies inside [1 - delta, 1 + delta]
FAILED if Q is disjoint from [1 - delta, 1 + delta]
UNRESOLVED otherwise, reported without a direction
verdicts.coverage: pointwise 95 % intervals; no simultaneous coverage across the up to 20 verdicts is claimed
verdicts.forced_incompatibility: Ki and Kj cannot both validate at a point iff Ki/Kj lies outside [(1 - delta)/(1 + delta), (1 + delta)/(1 - delta)]

closure.roadmap_F: Primary comparator K1. F closes VALIDATED iff K1 is VALIDATED at E3, E4 and E5. F closes FAILED iff E3, E4 and E5 all receive VALIDATED or FAILED for K1 and at least one is FAILED. Otherwise F remains OPEN.
closure.licensed_K1: only at the validated tuples (C, s, u, c/tau_c), within +/- delta, pointwise
closure.licensed_K2: a statement about the lag-1-matched fit only at the tuples where K2 is VALIDATED
closure.C08_boundary: reported separately: a finite-window binary-likelihood statement at C08's boundary requires E1 and E2 both evaluated and the comparator VALIDATED at both; otherwise that validation remains open, whatever F's closure
closure.diagnostics: K3 FAILED is a rate comparison consistent with note 27; the covariance defect is established algebraically and does not depend on it. K4 verdicts are not finite-window truth statements.

wording.before_evaluation: C08's archived mid-fringe implementation divides the exact first-lag binary correlation by F(u). Its four quoted thresholds survive a lag-1-fit correction on the stated coarse grid, but the archived rate map is not the finite-window comparator. Binary-likelihood validation remains confined to C04's tested point-sampled exact-r_k comparator; F remains open.
wording.c08_fact: C08's archived mid-fringe implementation divides the exact first-lag binary correlation by F(u). Its four quoted thresholds survive a lag-1-fit correction on the stated coarse grid, but the archived rate map is not the finite-window comparator.
wording.scope_without_finite_window_validation: Binary-likelihood validation of the exact-r_k comparator remains confined to C04's tested point-sampled cases.
wording.scope_with_finite_window_validation: The exact-r_k comparator (K1) is validated against the exact finite-window ARMA(1,1) binary likelihood within +/- 5 % (pointwise 95 % intervals) at {validated_tuples}. At every other input its binary-likelihood validation remains confined to C04's tested point-sampled cases.
wording.tuple_report: K1 at the mandatory points: VALIDATED at {validated}; FAILED at {failed}; UNRESOLVED or without a verdict at {other}.
wording.assembly: before evaluation: before_evaluation, verbatim. After evaluation: c08_fact; then scope_with_finite_window_validation if K1 is VALIDATED at any mandatory point, otherwise scope_without_finite_window_validation; then the status sentence for roadmap_F; then tuple_report. Tuples are written (C, s, u, c/tau_c) = (...). The campaign status never determines the scope sentence.

closure.post_unblinding: any analysis not specified here is labelled post-unblinding and cannot change a verdict

budget.aggregate_clock: the sum of wall-clock seconds recorded by every sid_run13 phase (numerical checks, pilots and evaluations) in its res13 artifact; each run reads the remaining budget from those records before it starts
budget.gate3_deadline: enforced from the start of the Gate-3 run for every step, including NC1, NC3 and the first point's measurement, and never later than the remaining aggregate budget; a step reaching it is stopped and recorded INCOMPLETE, and an incomplete NC1 blocks every point
budget.gate3_admission: before each point's NC2, NC4-NC6 and pilot, predict their cost from the measured t_step (the first point is run to measure it, within the deadline) and mark the point NOT_ATTEMPTED if the prediction exceeds the time left before the deadline; E1 and E2 are admitted together
budget.stop_rule: every evaluation run stops at start + min(stop_margin x predicted_seconds, point_cap_seconds, remaining aggregate seconds at its start); a stopped run is INCOMPLETE and receives no verdict

seeds.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(seed) (PCG64); one generator per (phase, point, replicate)

execution_stack.platform: osx-arm64, native; an osx-64 environment under Rosetta is a different stack and is not permitted
execution_stack.channel_policy: conda-forge only: both the solve and the installation pass --override-channels -c conda-forge with the same spec file, so configured channels such as defaults cannot enter either step
execution_stack.blas: OpenBLAS, pinned in the spec as libblas=*=*openblas
execution_stack.superseded_solve: analysis/stack_F/conda-dry-run-osx-arm64.json (python=3.12 without a patch pin resolved to 3.12.0)
stop_conditions: the installed conda package set (name, version, build) differs from the reviewed dry-run solve; channel metadata can change between the two steps
the solve or installation takes any package from a channel other than conda-forge
any conda package's subdir is neither osx-arm64 nor noarch
libblas's build string does not contain openblas
python is not 3.12.14, or numpy is not 2.4.4, or scipy is not 1.17.1
the installed python binary is not arm64
pip would install, upgrade or remove a distribution already provided by conda, or a pip report entry lacks a sha256
execution_stack.threads: OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS, MKL_NUM_THREADS, VECLIB_MAXIMUM_THREADS and NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS all equal 1, set before numpy is imported
execution_stack.recorded: python patch version, platform.machine(), numpy build configuration, libblas and libopenblas build strings, thread variables, git revision, protocol digest
execution_stack.refusal: sid_run13.py refuses a dirty tree, a python other than 3.12.14, numpy or scipy other than the pins, a machine other than arm64, a libblas build without openblas, any thread variable other than 1, a DRAFT status or a digest mismatch
execution_stack.timing: all locks are committed before Gate 3

design_evidence.record: deterministic quantities computed by the builder on the drafting stack; the execution stack must reproduce them
